column14: Table S2: List of specimens in the Welker Wisconsin Collection, arranged alphabetically by common names of species. The specimen numbers designate the year of acquisition by the first two digits, followed by a hyphen and 1 to 3 digits denoting the order in which the specimens were acquired. column14: Table S3: List of specimens in the Johnson Michigan State Collection, arranged in approximate phylogenetic order, according to the Universal Species Identification System.5 The specimen numbers for the Michigan State Collection carry the following information. The first two digits represent the year of acquisition. The third digit gives some information about the purpose of acquiring the specimen – 0 is a normal marsupial or monotreme specimen, 1 is an experimental specimen, 2 is a normal specimen, 3 is a cat, 4 is an opossum, and 5 is a raccoon. The last two digits represent the sequence during that year in which the specimen was acquired. Thus 65063 indicates a normal monotreme or marsupial specimen, the 63rd specimen acquired in 1965.

UPDATE proposal for the existing Sheet1 row (Item name Mink_etal_1981_TABLE1). Only the descriptive columns N-AH are proposed; A and D repeat what is already there so the paste is harmless, and B and E-M are left blank because they are formula/generated.

TAXON (cell was blank). Proposed 'Vertebrates (42 species: 3 fishes, 3 amphibians, 2 reptiles, 6 birds, 28 mammals)'. Reasoning: the printed table has exactly 42 animal rows and no blank or section rows, which matches the RESULTS statement that ratios 'for 42 vertebrate species are presented in Table 1'. The class split was counted from the printed taxon names and reproduces the paper's own arithmetic independently: 3+3+2 = 8 cold-blooded and 6+28 = 34 warm-blooded, exactly the 'eight cold-blooded vertebrates' and '34 warm-blooded vertebrates' the DISCUSSION counts. 19 of the 42 rows are genus-level ('Bufo sp', 'Pongo sp', 'Bos sp', ...), so a species-level taxon list is not available from this table.

DATA ROLE (cell was blank). Proposed 'secondary'. Reasoning: every value in the table is either taken from one of the paper's 92 cited references or computed by the authors from such values using their own equations. Columns A (body weight), B (brain weight) and D (body weight of the metabolism specimen) carry a printed reference number on all 42 rows; column C (spinal cord weight) carries one on 26 of 42 and a footnote letter on the other 16; columns F and G (brain and spinal metabolic rate) carry a reference number on only 5 and 3 rows respectively, the remainder being predictions from the paper's Eqs. 1, 3 and 4; and H, I, J, K and the metabolic ratio are arithmetic on those columns (footnotes e-i). The single primary component is three cells: footnotes j, m and n report the authors' OWN direct observation of a cord-to-brain weight percentage (Carassius auratus 14%, Rana catesbiana 79.6%, Squalus acanthias 70%) with no source cited, supplying column C for the Goldfish, Bullfrog and Shark rows - but even those percentages are applied to a cited brain weight. 'both' is therefore arguable on three cells out of the whole table; 'secondary' is the honest call and keeps the item out of the merges, which is the right outcome. If the owner prefers to surface those three cells, change to 'both' and merge only spinal_cord_weight for those rows.

CAUTION for any future merge: columns F and G are model predictions on 37 and 39 of 42 rows and must never be merged as measured metabolic rates.

column36: Data role = SECONDARY. Every macroanatomical column is re-used data: left V1 / left LGN / neocortex / brain mass = deSousa_etal_2010_Table1 (the same 9 specimens; audited 31 match, 1 mismatch, 4 one-sided within print precision); optic nerve cross-sectional area + eye half surface area = Stephan & Frahm 1981 species means (footnote f); human neocortex = MacLeod unpublished combined-sex mean n = 8 (footnote b); ptd brain+body mass = Herndon et al. 1999 (footnote d); Homo body mass = Zilles 1972 (a); Pan paniscus body mass = Jungers & Susman 1984 (c); EQ = derived (Martin 1981 / Ruff et al. 1997). The paper's own primary measurements (GLI values, relative laminar widths) are published only in Figures 5-7 and are not tabulated, and Tables 2-4 are derived statistics, so nothing here is ingested into a merge. Why the item is still worth having: it prints left V1 and left LGN in whole mm3 where 2010 Table 1 prints 1-d.p. cm3, and it confirms Macaca fascicularis ma22 left LGN = 46 mm3, which 2010 printed as 0 and the project had reconstructed as 0.046 cm3 from Supp. Table 2. All nine specimens resolve to the collection catalog (CAT-070, 080, 082, 095, 111, 131, 133, 134, 150) with printed sex and age matching. See deSousa_etal_2009_Table1.ReadMe.md.
